messages.subject: Multiple surveys over time
parts:
Hello,

I am helping to design a survey of a small area where the available effort and spacing considerations will allow the placement of about 12 to 15 transects. The survey will be repeated monthly over a 6 month period, with one of the objectives being to look at seasonal change in density.

The survey will be designed in DISTANCE using equal spaced parallel lines.

My expectation is that we will have to use a pooled detection function for all the surveys, given the expected number of sightings per survey. However this should not be problematic as the same platform and observers will be used throughout.

My question is this: is it better to use a new realization of the design (i.e. different transects) for every survey, or to use the same one each time? My expectation is that it is better to use a new realization each time, so that encounter rate is independent for each survey, but there may be factors I am not considering. It is logistically inconvenient to change the design for each survey, so I would like to make sure it is the correct approach.

Thanks in advance,

Daniel Pike.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Multiple surveys over time
parts:
Daniel

You are on the low side for replicate transects as you know.  Nonetheless, the question you ask is a common one.

There is a bit of information on the subject in Section 7.8.3 of Buckland et al. (2001).

By placing survey effort in new locations each month, you are accomplishing better spatial representation in your repeated surveys.  However, this comes at the expense of adding spatial variability to the temporal variability you are trying to measure.

If your objective is *solely* monthly changes in density, then using new realisations will make monthly differences more difficult to detect because of the added spatial variability induced by the changing transect locations.  However, given you stated seasonal changes were "one of the objectives", I suspect there are further objectives that need to be weighed in the decision.
